report: 41-year-old woman with 4 months of bilateral groin/right buttock pain, limited passive hip motion, positive right SLR, and low JOA scores. MRI subchondral T1 low-signal line/STIR hyperintensity and low femoral-neck BMD raise AVN/insufficiency fracture, but absent trauma/steroids/alcohol and prior fractures make classic AVN less likely. Overall, chronic bilateral mechanical symptoms most strongly support bilateral hip OA/dysplasia. Insufficiency fracture remains the main alternative.
